message: Warming audit: fixed 5 grouped issues (#98-#102) — scheduling/ban-risk, board indicators, cycle resilience, localization, channel feedback — plus 6 review-found bugs (reconcile aborting quarantine recovery, cap=1 lockout, trust-ceiling progress, one-sided faded-pair DMs, case-sensitive invite dedup, stale doc). 536 tests green, coverage>=90%.

PR #104 accounts QA audit: fixed 15 findings. H2/M1 — single-source RU localization (service emits raw AccountStatus + RU relative time; UI _account_status_label is the only translation point; deleted English _status_label). H1 — UI sends username=None when unchanged (no USERNAME_NOT_MODIFIED). H3 — error snapshots no longer cached. M2 footer hides only on success; M3 story kind inferred from extension (dropdown removed); M4 delete errors translated; M5 search debounce; M6 uploader CSS scoped to .tb-profile-dialog. All gates green, +6 tests (543 pass).
Нейрокомментинг: дизайн прогрилен (grill), архитектурное решение в decisions.md; на трекере созданы 4 milestone (Ф0-Ф3) + 7 issues #113-119 (Ф0 спайк-гейт + Ф1 MVP).

Ф1 neurocomment (#114-#119) смёржен в main: 6 стек-PR #122->#127, squash снизу вверх, каждый CI-зелёный (lint/ty/pytest-strict/aislop/semgrep/pip-audit). #124<->#126 is_forward add/add (squash стёр общую #116-историю) разрешён тривиально — листенер/схема/тест byte-identical к смёрженному листенеру, поэтому #126 лёг как verified engine-only diff. Живая канарейка (#119) и решение капчи (#120) оставлены оператору (HITL), не запускались.

neurocomment Ф2 #136: un-assign реализован repo-direct (remove_account_from_campaign — hard DELETE m2m, scoped по паре, no cascade т.к. readiness шарится между кампаниями), БЕЗ сервиса: тонкий campaign-CRUD идёт через core.db напрямую как assign/link/deactivate; pass-through-сервис был бы shallow-модулем (grill-решение, оператор делегировал выбор).

neurocomment Ф2 #136 (branch claude/peaceful-bhabha-e08f72, НЕ в main по просьбе оператора): un-assign аккаунта + мультикампанийный ui.select-переключатель. test-first (grill→tdd). 796 тестов зелёные, ruff/ty/aislop/format чисто, branch-cov >=90%. Пост-ревью 3 субагентами: без blocker/major; убраны 2 минорные избыточности (per-switch on_disconnect accumulation, redundant listener-null guard).

neurocomment #136 пост /code-review (max-effort): 2 громкие находки опровергнуты source-verify NiceGUI 3.13 (set_options сам чистит stale-value → listener-guard лишний; section.refresh пробросил бы event → on_switch wrapper нужен). Исправлены 2 минорных (дефолт переключателя -> campaigns[-1]; восстановлен on_disconnect-teardown таймера = конвенция репо). 1 major altitude: per-campaign Start/Stop поверх fleet-global слушателя -> caption-mitigation + follow-up #137 (вынос контролов на уровень флота). 796 тестов зелёные.

neurocomment #137 (altitude из код-ревью): per-campaign Start/Stop поверх fleet-global слушателя -> вынес listener+Запустить/Остановить в единый _render_runtime_controls (рендер один раз, listener из всех аккаунтов); per-campaign секция = каналы+аккаунты+онбординг; on_toggle упрощён (убрана listener-sync связка). Реализовано в ветке (коммит 048c49a), Closes #137.

Make-it-real epic (design to backend) merged to main via PR #190 (squash 4088748): proxy pool, trust/device/spam, edit-card checks, phone-code login + logout/reset, warming card log, neuro feed/captcha/board, neuro settings wired into the engine, profile edit + photo upload, proxy-delete confirm + account-delete FK fix. CI 7/7 green. Remaining de-mock items (warmed list, pool assign from card, story/music posting, neuro comment text, manual captcha) tracked for a follow-up /goal session.

feat/finish-design-backend (#191): removed all remaining frontend mocks — warming graduation (promote/unpromote + warmed list), ready-card proxy/flag/trust, AccountEdit proxy assign, +Account wizard import+assign, .session/tdata dropzone, profile media (photos/stories/music via base64 view), NC comment text, captcha solver toggle->solver_enabled + Пройти->retry, delete-campaign/channel-x/edit-prompt, account-delete. No new migration. 852 backend + 111 FE tests; 6/7 CI green; semgrep red = pre-existing infra drift (separate task).

2026-07-10 audit session. ponytail-audit found the repo lean (no dead code/deps/debt). Targeted complexity refactor merged (#207): AccountEdit 1274->~85 and NeurocommentPage 1408->~570 split into co-located ui/ siblings; warming start_warming C17->A, _run_chat_step C12->B, _read_and_react 5-tuple->dataclass. Item 3 (telegram dispatchers) dropped as net-negative churn. Then a parallel bug audit + fixes merged (#209): 4 MED (warming target-gate skips quarantine/flood_wait, neurocomment in-flight dedup read live, set_account_photo 400 not 500, decode_session_claims rejects empty AUTH__SECRET) + 2 LOW hardening (tdata-zip streams+counts real bytes vs declared, phone_geo loguru %s->{}). 1071 tests green, CI 7/7. Deferred: daily-cap ~2x on mid-cycle restart -> issue #208; six other low findings judged not-worth-fixing.

2026-07-11 feature: phone-number authentication as a 3rd add-account method (branch phone-authentication). Reused the existing phone-code gateway/service/cache + request-code/submit-code endpoints (built for re-auth); only gap was creating an account from a bare number. Added phone on AccountCreate (persisted in _create_account), start_phone_login(phone,label?) (digits->account_id/session_name, duplicate->SessionAlreadyExistsError->409), POST /accounts/start-login. Add-account wizard got a 'Номер телефона' method + dynamic 2/3-step stepper: phone -> account created -> proxy (existing step 2) -> step 3 requests+confirms code (code+2FA), run AFTER proxy assignment so the first Telegram connect uses the account's proxy (operator-confirmed ordering). New log-event phone_login_started (ru/en). Gates green: 1086 pytest / 207 vitest.

2026-07-11 operator-reported warming-card UI session (PR #212). The step rail was decorative (cycles_completed % 6) and could show a fake 'forming report' (Otchet) live step with no timer. Made the rail reflect the real engine cycle: activeStage maps persisted last_action (set_online/join->subscribe, read, react->reactions, stories, send_dm->stories fold), waiting states (sleeping/flood_wait/quarantine)->pause+countdown, idle->start. Reordered STAGES to emission order (subscribe,read,reactions,stories,pause) because the rail renders by index and stories runs after reactions; dropped the fake report step + its ru/en i18n labels. Backend now emits a real stories progress step: maybe_watch_stories returns whether a view landed, run_one_cycle advances via _watch_stories_step only when it did, stories added to _loop._PROGRESS_STEPS between react and send_dm. Grill caught the original premise error (current_phase is the multi-day lifecycle, not the in-cycle step). +2 backend / +6 vitest; 1081 pytest + 211 vitest + ruff/ty/tsc/eslint/steiger green. Sonnet 5 review clean over both increments.

2026-07-13 operator-reported warming-card fix (PR #236, merged 45f5e6e). A freshly-queued account showed a blinking «Подписка на каналы» during the cold-start wait (up to cold_start_spread_hours ~24h before the first cycle) — the engine was idle-sleeping, not subscribing. Loop now persists the computed first-run time to next_run_at (new _persist_cold_start_schedule, generation-CAS guarded so a restart resumes the same wait). Card detects the pre-start hold (active + cycles_completed==0 + no last_action) and shows «Выдержка перед стартом» + real live countdown, step rail idle until the first action. Operator chose the real countdown over a flat 24h. +2 backend / +1 vitest; subagent review clean. Same PR also fixed unrelated red CI (fresh CVEs): pillow 12.2.0->12.3.0 (lockfile bump, clears 5 CVEs); click PYSEC-2026-2132 unfixable (semgrep pins click~=8.1.8) so accepted via pip-audit --ignore-vuln + aislop _ACCEPTED_VULN_DEPS, both documented to drop once semgrep loosens its pin. Follow-up idea: move semgrep out of the runtime-audited dep set (uvx) to actually patch click.

Hardening batch (PR #264): reuse one per-account account_lock across warming+NC start/stop + session/tdata imports to close lifecycle/import races; NC flood/slow-mode cooldowns persisted via migration #34 and rehydrated on startup (durability, deliberately NOT an outbox); proxy assign/unassign/remove/rotate now evict the pooled Telethon client; account delete purges neurocomment_cooldowns + unlinks the .session; uploads rejected by size before read.

Neurocomment still loses posts on overload/idle/restart — no persistent incoming-post queue or catch-up; send↔DB idempotency reconciliation and backup readiness/off-site remain deferred (architecture, not patchable).

Warming cards show full account identity (name + phone/flag + profile photo) via shared entities/account helpers (accountDisplayName/accountInitials/AccountAvatar); WarmingAccountState & WarmedAccount now carry first_name/last_name/avatar_etag (#267/#268).
Session check now detects frozen Telegram accounts (authorized + get_me succeeds) via help.getAppConfig freeze_since_date + FrozenMethodInvalidError; adds permanent 'frozen' status (#266).

PR #272: account profile editing hardened after dual-agent audit. Stable error codes for profile/media edits (mirrors _channels.py table) instead of raw Telethon text; frozen/flood_wait status persisted at edit time via narrow update_account_status (session-check writer needs a fake TelegramSessionCheckResult, so not reused); avatar thumb/etag refreshed right after photo mutations; partial-success sync re-reads confirmed profile only on failure path (zero happy-path RPC). Deferred deliberately: premium bio 140 (needs premium detection), duplicate toast suppression (needs query-client meta), slow_mode/peer_flood do not change account status (per-chat limits).

Post-merge audit of PR #272 (two independent reviewers + adversarial verify): sticky flood_wait was breaking warming (readiness requires alive, reconcile parks warming in error) — flood_wait DB write now gated to the 9 profile/media edit action types, frozen stays global; status writes made best-effort so execute never raises on SQLite lock; _sync_confirmed_profile wrapped best-effort (live 4-char NFT usernames fail our schema and must not mask the real error code); flood_wait retry seconds arrive as strings on the wire (fields: dict[str,str]) — SPA parses instead of expecting a number; global mutation toast now translates stable codes. Media split reconciled onto operator's PR #275 (_media_stories.py) — our redundant _avatar.py split discarded, _profile.py kept for the _actions.py size budget.

Neurocomment anti-freeze + scale (#270, PR #276): pace every channel-join site + break on FloodWait; persisted rolling-24h per-account join cap (default 20); already_participant no-ops not counted; listener join pass moved to single-flighted background task off the request/lock path; per-post hot path scoped to O(campaign candidates); peer-id cache + bulk sweep bucketing. Deferred: listener sharding at ~500 channels/account, Postgres for concurrent write scale.

Merge-conflict resolution #276 vs #274 (both restructured neurocomment onboarding): migration 35 kept for main's add_neurocomment_challenges_channel_index (merged first), #276's add_neurocomment_join_log renumbered to 36 — tests derive versions from MIGRATIONS dynamically so renumbering is safe. Both PRs extracted the same pair helpers into different modules (_onboard_pair.py in main, _classify.py in #276); kept main's structure — _onboard_pair.py owns the pair helpers — but it imports _classify_join/_solve_and_record from _classify.py instead of duplicating. _classify.py got #274's rate_limited→llm_rate_limited handling grafted in while keeping #276's already_participant-counts-as-ok fix; _at_join_cap + record_join moved into _onboard_pair.py with a re-export from onboarding so _join.py and _onboard_channel.py imports stay unchanged.

cold_start_spread_hours stays 5, operator decision 2026-07-25: a short time-to-first-cycle beats avoiding night-time starts. The ceiling wins over the active-hours snap, and the two cannot both hold — the snap only ever moves a candidate FORWARD to the account's next local morning, so it fits under the ceiling only when the spread exceeds the quiet window (9h at active_hours 8-23) plus active_hours_start_spread_minutes, i.e. ~13h. Measured at 5h: the snap survives ~4% of cold starts and ~37% begin inside the account's local night (100% for a +52 fleet started during Moscow morning, since 08:00-12:00 MSK is 23:00-03:00 local). Live symptom that forced this: two accounts started 02:34 UTC sat at cycles_completed=0 with next_run_at 16:35/17:25, a 14h wait. Do not 'fix' the night starts without asking — they are paid for deliberately. The ceiling covers the first cycle only; a persisted next_run_at is honoured verbatim, so a stop+start is what re-rolls an account already waiting.

phase_daily_cap intro and settling both 15, operator decision 2026-07-25, accepting the safety-ramp cost. The cap does double duty: persona_next_run_seconds affords cap // expected_actions_per_session (5) sessions and splits the 15h active window between them, so 15 is the ALGEBRAIC MINIMUM for the requested ~5h inter-cycle pause (3 sessions, 3.75-6.25h measured). At the old intro=3 that floored to one session and a ~15h gap, matching the live rows exactly (cycle 03:01:43 -> next_run_at 17:14:21 = 14.21h). settling had to follow intro up because test_compute_intensity_monotonic_in_age forbids the cap dropping as an account ages. Accepted costs, all confirmed: day-1 volume is 5x the old value in the highest-risk window; phase_hard_floor_age_hours (24) becomes a no-op because the phase drives ONLY the daily cap (channel counts, reaction probability and the DM gate are phase-independent); and _TRUST_PHASE_CEILING['critical'] = 'settling' means a degraded account of any age now gets 15/day instead of 10. Also fixed here: at cap 3 the DM step and the story glance were structurally unreachable, because the cycle spends its budget in a fixed order (set_online counts, then joins/reads, then stories, then the DM) — which is why inter-account dialogue had produced zero messages. The clean way to shorten the pause without raising the safety ceiling is to decouple sessions/day from the cap in persona_next_run_seconds; proposed, not done.

Warming DM peers resolve via contacts.resolvePhone, not contacts.importContacts. Both sit behind the same inputPrivacyKeyAddedByPhone gate so reach is identical, but importContacts writes a permanent saved contact and nothing in the repo ever deletes one. With partners reshuffling every dialogue_reshuffle_days at degree ~4-6, every account would accumulate a contact list consisting exclusively of other fleet accounts, largely mutual — a stronger server-side correlation tell than the ones _fleet.py channel slicing and the audit #203 subset cut already defend against. Verified on Telethon 1.44.0 that a contacts.ResolvedPeer still populates the session entities table via _call's process_entities, so the access_hash caching is unchanged.

An unaddressable DM partner skips the turn instead of failing the cycle. A cycle with status=failed and no work done sends the account to the terminal error state (_transitions.py), so one partner whose phone-lookup privacy hides them would kill an otherwise healthy sender — and keep killing it after every operator restart. DmPeerUnresolvedError therefore returns failures=0 with attempted_actions=1: no park, but the RPCs still bill against the daily cap rather than running off-budget beside it. The counterpart constraint is that ONLY permanent conditions may map to that class. Telethon collapses exhausted retries into a bare ValueError, and briefly catching it (df0b008) meant a datacentre wobble consumed a live unanswered partner message via mark_message_replied while reporting the cycle ok. Deliberately NOT exempting send_dm from the terminal-error transition: a DM failing in a cycle that achieved nothing else is real evidence, and hiding it would turn the board amber.

A silently dropped bio is reported from the modal's post-save live pull, not from a server-side re-read that persists the confirmed value. The persisting design was built first and rejected on audit: accounts.bio is read nowhere but this modal's initial form default, which the live re-seed overwrites on open, so it fixed no visible divergence; and under replication lag the confirmation read answers with the pre-write value, writing a bio Telegram does not hold into a column no other writer heals. The verdict is therefore derived from the pull rather than stored, so a lagged read clears itself on the next one, and it is gated on the pull having settled and succeeded because a stale or refused read is not evidence.

Mutation testing is only as honest as the fixtures. A deleted re-seed guard 'survived' every mutant because the fetch mock returned byte-identical payloads for the plain and forced snapshot reads: TanStack Query structurally shares them, the query data keeps its identity, and the useEffect watching it never re-runs. The guard was removed on that evidence and an audit caught it. When a test must exercise an effect keyed on query data, vary a field the assertion does not care about.
logs: per-domain event prefixes; warming card filters warming_,telegram_,spam_status; neurocomment feed now carries the Telegram error_type; LIKE escaping closed a whole-table purge hazard (PR #298)

Profile bio cap stays 70, premium 140 stays deferred. PR #299 considered raising it and reversed: .mex/events/decisions.jsonl records PR #272 deferring it on purpose pending premium detection, and 140 is the premium ceiling only. A flat raise trades a free local check for a metered account.updateProfile RPC per attempt on the majority of accounts, and makes AboutTooLongError -> about_too_long load-bearing for the common case while it had no test at all. Added that missing gateway test instead. Finishing it properly needs per-account premium detection, which session_io already captures as extra[is_premium] and appConfig exposes as about_length_limit_default/premium.

parse_mode disabled globally on the pooled Telegram client, markdown stripped from generated text only. Telethon defaults to markdown and it was silently eating paired markers and links from operator-authored channel posts; the list read then fed the stripped text back into the edit form, so re-saving made the damage permanent. parse_mode is not a constructor argument, so it is set as an attribute on both return branches of create_telegram_client. Verified none of the 10 send sites relied on markdown. Consequence: LLM text on the two human-mimicking surfaces started arriving with literal asterisks, and no prompt forbids markup, so strip_markdown_delimiters runs on generated text and never on operator text - a deterministic strip beats a prompt instruction we cannot enforce. It only removes PAIRED delimiters, because Telethon never italicised foo__bar either.

Narrow lint rule for the useMutation callback class, not a broad ban. One useMutation is one callback slot: a second mutate(), a reset(), or unmounting takes it over and the first call's handler never runs while the request still completes server-side. That cost seven bugs in the account-editing audit (a story published twice, a wizard forgetting an account it created, two .session imports sharing one status, a dropped onImported, a swallowed post-list refresh, a swallowed campaign-link result, a proxy assign advancing before it resolved). Seven recurrences means sweeping by inspection does not converge. Measured before choosing: a broad no-inline-mutate-callbacks rule flags 51 sites across 23 files and most are correct, so it would be suppressed everywhere and be worse than nothing. Shipped no-restricted-syntax for mutate() inside a loop callback only - unambiguously wrong, zero suppressions, and it catches the worst instance we actually had. The rest is a written rule in context/frontend.md and a review question.

log_event extra must carry bounded values only, enforced by an AST gate, and stdlib logging is bridged into loguru to keep retention. extra is not log-only: it is persisted as JSON and served by GET /logs and streamed by GET /events, so 22 sites putting str(exc) in it were publishing proxy URLs with credentials and absolute .session paths. Rejected a redaction pass over extra - heuristic redaction is false security and hides the rule; bounded at the call site where the author can see the value. Moving the text to the stdlib logger would have cost retention, because uvicorn's LOGGING_CONFIG has no root key so records fell to lastResort and lived only in stderr; root is bridged into the rotating loguru sink instead, file-only, and lastResort is re-added explicitly because adding any handler silences it. The gate is deliberately precise over strict: zero false positives across 371 files matters more than coverage, since a fence needing an allowlist at every corrected site is worse than none. Its docstring says it is a drift guard, not a proof, and names what it cannot see.

Captcha queue hides unactionable rows instead of badging them (PR #328). Hide, not grey out: a dead row with a disabled button is a second list needing its own triage, which is the problem being fixed. Hidden are banned (#30), operator-skipped (#148), out of chat with the re-join budget spent, channel serving a #147 pause, and anything past challenge_queue_max_age_days (3). The reason is NOT that onboarding refuses them: retry_pair DELETES the readiness row before onboarding, so every guard keyed on that row is skipped and the retry really does re-join and re-solve. That is why the rows must go - the click would lift a ban #30 calls permanent, undo the operator's own skip, or spend a join RPC Telegram already refused four times while resetting rejoin_attempts to zero. Only the pause is truly unreachable (returns before the join RPC). Budget uses _rejoin.exhausted, not access_lost alone: a pair still inside its budget stays listed because the sweep may put it back in the chat. Every exclusion must be inside the one SQL statement - filtering after LIMIT let 24 hidden rows (six pairs, four challenge rows each) fill a 20-row page and hide the one actionable pair.

The board badge and the captcha queue read one table and are ALLOWED to disagree (PR #328). The badge answers 'why is this channel stuck', the queue 'what can a human press today'. They share exactly one exclusion, _still_blocked, because the table is append-only and a long-resolved give_up made _channel_status report bot_challenge for a channel Telegram was write-blocking - naming the wrong wall. They deliberately do NOT share the age window or the skip exclusion: applying either there would report chat_restricted for a channel a bot gate really is holding, and ChannelStatus has no value carrying the truth instead. Do not 'finish the job' by aligning them.

Grounded the pattern library (12 to 27 nodes over 11 files): mex impact reads only the grounded-source table, so ungrounded notes are invisible to the one command that answers which memory a change invalidates. Followed mex's own split - patterns and deep-domain ground tightly, architecture/conventions stay ungrounded - not a coverage target, which mex explicitly forbids.

Grounded the pattern library, 12 to 27 nodes over 11 files. Reason: mex impact reads only the grounded-source table, so an ungrounded note is invisible to the one command that answers which memory a code change invalidates. Followed mex's own split - patterns and deep-domain ground tightly, architecture/conventions/setup stay ungrounded - which is a rule about WHICH files, not a coverage target; mex explicitly forbids grounding just so every file has an entry, and has no coverage metric at all. Grounding add-service exposed a false claim: tests/test_architecture.py never verified that public I/O is async and typed.

A give-up verdict is FINAL: only a deliberate act unmakes it, never the clock (PR #333). Reporting a give-up is a claim to the operator that nothing is working on the pair any more, and the re-join budget's staleness rule quietly withdrew that claim every 48h - the pair re-joined and re-solved forever while the clamped log reprinted '2/2' each round and rejoin_attempts climbed past the budget it was printing. exhausted() therefore answers on the verdict BEFORE it looks at the counter, so the board badge, the sweep and the captcha queue all read one rule instead of three. The staleness rule stays, but only for pairs that never gave up: a spent counter proves nothing about a pair whose budget shrank under it. The two ways back are acts, not time - a real re-join, and the operator re-linking the channel - and re-link now also clears the captcha flags, which it did not, so a re-linked channel used to inherit an invisible give-up. Corollary in the same PR: giving up no longer leaves the chat. The state that says the pair is out of the chat is the same state a leave would act on, so the leave was two RPCs spent to leave a chat we are not in - and for a pair we ARE in, membership costs nothing. Do not 'fix' the wording back to a leave: the log now says the account is no longer in the channel, which is what the state actually knows.

A write refusal names WHOSE restriction it is before anything acts on it (PR #333). Telegram returns the same refusal whether the chat mutes everyone (default_banned_rights) or this one account is restricted in it (participant banned_rights + until_date), and the old code read both as 'the channel forbids comments'. That charged a personal mute to the channel: the other accounts were paused out of a chat they post in fine, and the channel spent a round toward an unlink nobody earned. So a probe now answers a SCOPE - everyone / self_only / none / unknown - and only 'everyone' may reach the channel-level rule. 'self_only' parks that one pair until muted_until on the persisted per-pair cooldown (#34), not a module dict, because a mute outlives restarts; the readiness row alone would not hold it, since the next onboarding pass re-joins as already_participant, finds no challenge, writes 'ready' back, and the pair's next refusal spends the CHANNEL a round. The wait is bounded by the same channel_pause_hours * channel_max_rounds every sibling rule counts out - a permanent restriction carries no date at all and a date years out is no more useful, so both fall back to that bound and are simply re-armed by the next refusal. Nobody leaves the chat over a write block: membership costs nothing and re-joining would spend the rolling-24h join cap. 'unknown' stays unknown rather than guessing the harsher branch.

Neuroshilling got its own routed context instead of a section inside neurocomment's (PRs #363-#381). The two share an account-ownership registry, a join budget and the outbound content filter, but they are separate runtimes with separate start paths, and folding either into the other's route would make every neurocomment task load shilling prose and every shilling task load neurocomment's. Contexts went from 8 to 9 of the 12 CI allows, so nothing had to be squeezed to make room, and the always-loaded anchor gained one word naming the feature. What went into the context is the reasoning the code does not carry: mutual exclusion across warming, neurocomment and neuroshilling through one identity-keyed registry that the neurocomment LISTENER is deliberately not a holder of; the daily join cap shared with neurocomment because Telegram counts joins per account and not per feature; text dedup scoped to the target, and to the cycle in revive, because replaying one approved dialogue is the feature rather than an accident of it; the autoreply boundary being the parser over the string that would be sent, with the prompt fence as depth behind it; and the outbound filter being warming's own list with no neuroshilling copy, asked again at approval so the operator is told before a run finishes having skipped every message step. Left out as derivable: generation clearing the operator's media step, which is one local write whose own comment explains it.

The red MEX job was one GROUNDING_DRIFT, not the seventeen STALE_FILE warnings printed beside it. The neuroshilling merge added a reaction arm and a media-copy arm to the write dispatcher that add-telegram-task grounds, so its body hash moved; locally the check stayed green because a machine without a built graph silently skips every grounding check. Re-read against the new body, the note's claim still held, but the body showed something the note glossed over: the dispatcher matches concrete action MODELS rather than action_type because that is what narrows the type inside an arm, and it ends in a prefix-matched channel family plus a profile-media default, so a forgotten arm does not report an unsupported action, it raises out of profile-media. Wrote that in and then re-captured, which is the only order the gate accepts: a re-capture whose memory file did not change is refused, precisely so a stale sentence cannot be shipped behind a refreshed hash.

Twelve STALE_FILE warnings were left standing rather than cleared by bumping last_updated on notes that are still true. mex derives that code from the file's position in the WHOLE repository's commit list, so nineteen merged PRs pushed every routed file past the threshold at once and the only thing that resets a counter is a commit touching the file. Re-read each of the twelve: the layer law, the backend and frontend rules, the pattern index and the add-service, add-api-endpoint, add-auth, add-log-event, add-frontend-slice, add-discovery-source and add-warming-job patterns say nothing the new feature falsified, and no repeatable workflow emerged from it worth a pattern file of its own. A metadata-only touch would clear the counter while proving nothing, which is the fake freshness the scaffold exists to prevent and the exact reason the workflow keeps STALE_FILE non-blocking. They will clear on their own the next time a real change lands in each file.

The recovery-email path deliberately does NOT go through Telethon's edit_2fa, and this is the fact that cost the most to establish. edit_2fa builds new_password_hash = b'' whenever new_password is falsy, and a present-but-empty hash is not 'leave the password alone', it REMOVES the cloud password — so the obvious one-liner (call edit_2fa with only an email) would attach the address and wipe the account's password in the same request, silently, on the very feature whose reason for existing is that a lost session cannot be re-authorised without that password. Its email argument also demands an email_code_callback that reads the mailed code out of a mailbox, which an unattended backend has no way to do. So the email half issues the raw account.updatePasswordSettings with new_algo and new_password_hash OMITTED from the flags and only email set — what TDLib's set_recovery_email_address does — authorised with telethon.password.compute_check, and the operator types the code back in a second request instead of a callback. The tests assert both password fields are None on the wire, because that assertion is the whole guard between this feature and a silent password wipe. Corollary, learned the same way: EMAIL_UNCONFIRMED_<N> is that call's SUCCESS signal, not a failure — the address is attached and N is the mailed code's length — so it is caught and returned as pending rather than raised.

The cloud-password write issues account.updatePasswordSettings itself instead of calling Telethon's edit_2fa, and the reversal is not about style: edit_2fa can fail to return at all. compute_digest and compute_check both call telethon.password.check_prime_and_good, whose fast path fires only when the server's prime byte-equals Telethon's hardcoded one; any other p drops into Pollard-Brent factorisation OF a prime, which never terminates - measured still running past 30s on the RFC 3526 group-14 prime. p is a server-supplied field, so one Telegram prime rotation would wedge the single uvicorn worker permanently, taking warming, the neurocomment listener, SSE and /ready with it. Owning the RPC is what makes the SRP work ours to place: it runs under asyncio.to_thread with a 15s wait_for, so an expiry costs one failed request plus one leaked unkillable thread instead of the process - Python cannot kill a thread, and that is the accepted trade. Owning it also settled three costs of delegating. The pre-flight getPassword added last round closed only half the window it claimed, because edit_2fa re-read getPassword for itself: execute reports "may have been applied" for any failure after the client was borrowed, so a socket dying one leg later was still reported as a possibly-applied password. It made three getPassword calls where one will do, and it was the leg that ate a FLOOD_WAIT before anything was written. The reproduction is faithful to edit_2fa's body including salt1 += os.urandom(32), which is security-relevant rather than cosmetic, while the one deliberate empty new_password_hash is now written from the verb (new_password is None) rather than from a falsy default. The TypeError catch went with it: it existed only because edit_2fa calls a callback we never pass, and it was not gated on the verb, so a removal answered that way would have cleared the stored password for a removal that may not have happened.

Refuse a server-supplied input you cannot compute safely, instead of bounding the computation. Telethon's check_prime_and_good fast path fires only for its hardcoded prime AND a generator of 3/4/5/7, so a rotated prime - or that same prime with g of 2 or 6 - falls into Pollard-Brent factorisation OF a prime, which does not terminate (measured still running past 30s on the RFC 3526 group-14 prime). Both p and g are server-supplied, so the cloud-password gateway now admits the (p, g) pair via require_fast_algo BEFORE it offloads anything and refuses every other pair outright; that refusal, not a timeout, is what makes the non-terminating path unreachable. The surviving 15s bound is defence in depth against a future Telethon changing that fast path, not the guarantee. Bounding alone would have left the bad path reachable and merely time-boxed, which is the weaker property it was mistaken for. Second, and the reason the bound was itself a hazard: offloading is not isolation unless the pool is yours. The SRP work ran on asyncio.to_thread, i.e. the loop's DEFAULT executor, which in this app is the same pool every core.repositories call runs on (~450 to_thread call sites, none bounded). Measured on that arrangement: 20 expiries fill the executor and an ordinary repository call never runs; four leaked threads take event-loop lateness from 11ms to 182ms (the GIL, not one core); and asyncio.run's shutdown_default_executor JOINS the leaked worker, so a graceful shutdown hangs instead of exiting. A private two-worker ThreadPoolExecutor keeps all three off the database. Honest residual: Python cannot kill a thread, so an expiry still leaks one worker of two and interpreter exit's atexit join would wait on it - one process-exit hang rather than a wedged worker, a starved DB pool and a hung asyncio.run.

Narrowed fingerprint immutability to device identity only, so an imported account stops announcing en-US for life. The two import paths mint before any connection exists (the connect needs the fingerprint), so they cannot know the phone; the first alive session check may correct lang_code/system_lang_code once, gated in the WHERE clause on the row still carrying the fallback. Device columns stay immutable because a machine changing under its owner is a linkage signal, while a person changing their system language is not. Country->language comes from CLDR likelySubtags for every phonenumbers region rather than a hand-picked list, so the fallback now means 'no phone yet'.

Confined the language correction to an account's first session check, adding accounts.last_checked_at IS NULL to the WHERE clause beside the fallback guard. The fallback half alone was not enough: pre-existing rows drew lang_code and system_lang_code independently and no migration touches them, so a legacy ('ja','en-US') still looked like a fallback and would have been rewritten on some routine check months into the account's life, while ('ko','ru-RU') was never repairable anyway. Changing what an established account announces is the linkage signal this correction exists to remove, so the existing fleet is now out of scope entirely and keeps announcing what it announces today. Expressed as an EXISTS subquery rather than a hoisted Python read so both halves of the guard are still evaluated by the database at write time; the correction consequently runs BEFORE the accounts UPDATE that stamps last_checked_at, in the same transaction.

Dropped the accounts.last_checked_at IS NULL half of the language-correction guard, restoring the predicate to device_fingerprints.account_id plus system_lang_code == FALLBACK_TAG. The "first check" half did not mean what it read: last_checked_at is stamped by EVERY session check and by update_account_status, not by a successful one, so an account whose first check returned non-alive kept the en-US fallback permanently even after the operator fixed the proxy and re-checked - 8 of 200 in a bulk tdata import. The load-bearing case is worse and was demonstrated: with TELEGRAM__API_ID unset, core/telegram_client/_session.py answers session_error for every account before it opens a client, so one credential misconfiguration at import time silently cost a whole batch the feature for good; and .session import runs no session check at all, so a typed action stamping the column via update_account_status could exclude a row before anything had checked it. The trade the operator accepted for that: pre-existing rows drew lang_code and system_lang_code independently, so roughly 1 in 14 carries en-US beside an unrelated lang_code and will now be corrected on its next session check, changing the locale an established account announces. Judged the better outcome because such a pair is internally contradictory today - a per-account, single-observation tell - whereas a corrected pair is coherent; and because a synchronised fleet-wide flip is not reachable, there being no bulk-check route in the API and no multi-select in AccountsPage.tsx, so at most one account moves per operator action. Supersedes the rationale of the entry above it, which is kept so the record shows the rationale changed. The statement reorder that entry introduced is reverted with it: its only purpose was to read last_checked_at before the UPDATE stamped it, and both orderings are behaviourally identical inside the one transaction.

Listener pointer has two writers with one guard set. POST /neurocomment/listener persists the picked account only while the engine is stopped; a running engine is re-pointed by /start, because that is an ownership hand-off and only start reconciles it. Both paths run the same three busy checks (warming, discovery, neuroshilling) via _refuse_if_busy: a saved pointer is not inert, resolve_search_account prefers it for channel discovery whether or not the engine runs, so a pointer at a session another runtime owns would put a paced keyword stream on it.

The listener card deliberately does not name the listener account — only status and campaign count. The name lives in the edit modal alone. Operator's design choice, confirmed 2026-08-23; reviewers keep reporting it as a missing label. Do not add it.

Neither /neurocomment/start nor /neurocomment/listener checks that the picked account still exists, so a delete racing a save can leave the pointer naming a purged row (no FK on neurocomment_runtime.listener_account_id). Needs two clients inside one second; the fallout is a dead pointer that Start and discovery error on, cleared by one press of 'снять слушателя'. Deliberately left: fix both endpoints together when next editing them, not as its own task.

Board deletions are three numbers on purpose, not one duplicated. The row chip is one (account, channel) pair over posted comments, because it renders beside a channel name and that is what an operator reads it as. The channel pill is the whole channel over DELIVERED comments, a wider set that includes a comment recorded failed mid-send but actually live - it is the number that has to explain a back-off, and no account card can see it. The Udaleno tile is the account over every channel, and stays subset-of-comments because both come off the same posted rows. Collapsing any two loses a real case: the channel aggregate accused five accounts of one deletion, and the account total hung a deletion from another channel next to whichever channel the row happened to show.

A raw event code in the operator log meant a missing status suffix, not a missing translation. logEventTelegram.status.by_request had been in both locales all along; by_request was absent from the SPA's suffix list AND from the parity test's mirror of it, so four call sites rendered their event code while CI reported the family covered. Filtering the row out on the page was the wrong instinct and was reverted to a one-word fix in two lists. Only the neurocomment discussion-group row stays filtered, and only because _classify.py genuinely twins it with a translated line carrying the attempt ratio.

_onboard_pair runs ensure_current() between the join RPC and the _classify_join that stamps the request, and its CancelledError is a BaseException no handler on that path catches. A Stop landing in that window skips stamp_join_request, so the next pass does not see the request in flight and re-sends it - which the code elsewhere says an admin reads as spam. Pre-existing; PR 392 only removed its visible symptom (the untranslated gateway row).

Per-account cap overrides: NULL means follow the fleet, 0 means no cap. Nullable columns rather than defaults because zero is a real limit on the join and per-channel caps, so absence had to be spelled differently. One resolver serves every gate and the operator gauge so a shown cap is always the enforced cap. The join override governs neuroshilling too, since the budget it spends is the account's and not the feature's, while each feature keeps its own fleet default.

Bound the write model, never the model built from stored rows. A ceiling on AccountLimitOverride looked like defence in depth and was the worse bug: a stored row is data, not a request, and refusing to parse it does not undo it. The bulk override load builds one per candidate, so one out-of-range row would abort the whole selection pass plus both join gates and the GET, instead of affecting its own account. A CHECK cannot rescue this either, because a migration already stamped will not run again and editing one in place is forbidden.

The reset moment names the row whose ageing-out puts the window back UNDER the cap, which is the oldest row only while usage sits at the cap. Lowering a cap below current usage leaves used-cap rows that must age out first, and naming the oldest was hours early. The cap is therefore an argument to the window read, resolved against a count taken in the same transaction: a count read a moment earlier let a concurrent join pick the wrong row and reintroduce the same class of error.

A per-account table with no foreign key is only kept clean by two things, and both are easy to miss: _delete_account must purge it, and the write must refuse an unknown account inside its own transaction. neurocomment_account_limits shipped missing both; a reimported account under the same id inherited stale caps, and a stale max_joins_per_day=0 reads as no cap in BOTH neurocomment and neuroshilling.

Letter-spacing gets no scale. Four of the five values the app spends are already declared by the roles that need them (type-eyebrow carries 0.04em, type-page-title -0.02em), so a tracking-* rung would be a second way to say what the role says, and a scale nobody reaches for directly is worse than none. The one survivor, tracking-code (0.18em), is not typography: it is the spacing that lets a one-time code be read back character by character, and both wearers pair it with a spaced placeholder and strip the spaces before Telegram sees them. The wordmark's -0.01em is exempt rather than named, because it is a value the design source Telebuba.dc.html sets and a rule about typographic scales has no standing over a brand mark.

Body text gets no line-height rung, because preflight sets html{line-height:1.5} and the fontSize rungs are bare strings that do not override it — the app's ambient leading is already 1.5 everywhere. So the sixteen leading-[1.5] sites were restating an inherited value and were deleted rather than renamed, and a 'prose' rung would have finished the sweep with zero wearers. 1.45 was resolved to the inherited 1.5 on the config's own curve precedent, whose load-bearing half is two values meeting on one gesture: here they met on one component three times (the how-to step copy-pasted into three pages, the chat bubble in two, and Notice drawing itself at 1.5 while a caller passed 1.45 back in). Only two rungs survive — stack (1.25) for a heading over its own detail line, and log (1.85) for the monospace stream on a term surface. leading-none is not a text rung at all: all eight wearers are single glyphs.

Two clusters of hand-written buttons were folded onto existing Button rungs and neither earned a new one. The six pagination controls measured 0.75px from size=sm in a real browser — a third of the two pixels this component already ruled is drift rather than a decision — and nothing else in the app sets lead at weight 400. The five retry actions inside a danger Notice keep a white fill as a className override rather than a sixth variant: the fill is meaningful (variant=danger paints bg-danger-tint, which is exactly what the Notice under them already paints, so it would vanish), but all five wearers sit in one slice and the rule wants two. Measuring corrected the record: the ladder stated in Button.tsx and the canon (27/29/25) was computed at line-height 1.0, which this app has nowhere; the real heights are md 41.5 / sm 34.75 / refused-pill 32.5 / xs 30.75. The gaps the earlier refusal turned on survive; the absolutes did not.

No dark theme and no CSS-custom-property theming layer, deliberately. The strongest published argument for that indirection is not dark mode but making contrast changes in one place across several themes — and this app has one theme, has already done that work by hand twice (the deep rungs), and has no external consumers of its components. Rejected alongside cva (every variant prop here is typed as keyof typeof its own as-const record, so a key cannot drift from its type — the one thing cva adds is compoundVariants, and there are none), visual regression testing (it would not have caught a single one of the audit's thirteen findings: a 0s transition, a focus ring's contrast, an unresolvable ARIA reference and a missing reduced-motion block are all invisible to a screenshot), and generated props tables (the drift was in prose and in variant records; the second is now generated by a parser the repo already owned).

Replacing a Tailwind scale with names silently breaks tailwind-merge for that axis, and it has now happened three times. tailwind-merge knows the PREFIX but validates the VALUE, so a named rung it does not recognise joins no class group, conflicts with nothing, and survives beside its own opposite — the winner then decided by stylesheet order rather than by the caller's last word. It cost every filled Button its font size (text-*), then dropped line-heights and letter-spacing, then let a component beat its own caller's padding override in every cn-based component. Whenever a scale is replaced in tailwind.config.ts, cn.ts must be extended in the same change and a regression test added; a class that renders correctly today proves nothing, because the failure mode is alphabetical accident.

CI слушает только pull_request/push на main, поэтому у стекового PR ноль проверок и при этом mergeStateStatus CLEAN: защита ветки его не держит, потому что требуемый контекст физически не приходит. Порядок для стека: смержить родителя, перебазировать дочернюю ветку на main (squash разрывает её историю), дождаться CI, мержить.

Настройка, которую библиотека не читает, удаляется, а не правится. expect.toHaveScreenshot.timeout Playwright игнорирует: в логе CI стоял with timeout 30000ms при выставленных 10000. Опция с виду выглядит принятым решением, поэтому она хуже отсутствующей; срок для снимка задаётся только при вызове.

Эталоны снимков из артефакта CI переносятся по ПРОИСХОЖДЕНИЮ расхождения, а не по количеству: берутся те, чьё расхождение вызвано правкой. Обычно это упавшие; если менялся сам способ съёмки — весь затронутый набор. Применение правила по букве дало три прогона, в которых провал перемещался с одного снимка на другой из-за смешанного набора эталонов.

Форма контрола не приходит из ступени размера. Параметр shape у buttonBase удалён и не восстанавливается: единственный вызывающий передавал его из таблицы размеров, то есть параметр существовал ровно для того, чтобы размер мог менять форму. Кнопка — пилюля на всех ступенях, иконочная — квадрат rounded-md, круг только через shape=circle. Прежние объяснения исключений противоречили друг другу и счёту носителей.

Условный ребёнок в обходе исходников — не всегдашний кусок. Гейт контраста не читал stroke-/fill- потому, что попытку добавить их однажды откатили: на десяти парах разбор ошибался в четырёх. Одна причина — элемент, который САМ является глифом, не опознавался глифом (glyphOnly спрашивает, что элемент СОДЕРЖИТ, а у <Icon/> тело пусто), и его держали у пола 4.5:1 вместо 3:1. Вторая — условный ребёнок считался всегдашним и сходился с ОБЕИМИ половинами родительского тернарника, давая белое на белом 1.00:1. Закрыто через причину, а не симптом: пропускать пару с равными hex было бы одной строкой, но тогда гейт перестал бы ловить белое по белому — самую дорогую ошибку контраста, и ровно ту, что жила на кнопке проверки в таблице аккаунтов. Правило: не-всегда не встречается с не-всегда, та же семантика, что у ветвей шаблонного литерала. Цена названа в комментарии — пара «чернила на действии» в такой форме держится рукописным утверждением.

Рецепт забирает сведение состояний, а не только рунги. verdictFill вынес три рунга кнопки исхода (idle/ok/err), которые AccountsTable и ActionsSection собирали независимо. Первый вариант принимал только рунг, и тогда правило «запрос в полёте носит заливку покоя» осталось на обоих местах вызова — по тернарнику и по комментарию на каждом. Это правило той же природы, что и сами рунги: заливка отвечает на «каков ответ», а не на «идёт ли запрос». Порог: рецепт принимает СОСТОЯНИЕ вызывающего, если сведение состояния к рунгу — часть того же решения; иначе в общее уходит то, что совпадало, а снаружи остаётся то, что разошлось бы. Тип VerdictState объявлен в дизайн-системе, а не взят из shared/lib: импорт барреля замкнул бы recipes → lib → cn → tokens.

Аккаунт попадает в кампанию нейрошиллинга ТОЛЬКО через карточку роли; отдельного пикера ростера больше нет. Пикер спрашивал список аккаунтов, а роли раздавались вторым, ничем не связанным действием, поэтому «выбрал двоих» и «обе роли укомплектованы» были разными состояниями, и запуск отказывал между ними. Теперь «в кампании» и «играет роль» — одно и то же: выбор «Без аккаунта» выводит аккаунт из кампании, а назначение сперва снимает роль с прежнего исполнителя, иначе у одной роли оказывалось бы два, и укомплектованность (она считается множеством role_id) разницы бы не заметила. В списке предлагается ВЕСЬ пул, а занятый в другом месте показан выключенным вместе с тем, кто его держит: спрятать его значило бы оставить оператора гадать, почему аккаунта нет.

«Отмена» в диалоге настроек кампании ОТКАТЫВАЕТ оба черновика, пересевая их из серверных значений вместе с эталонами; Escape и клик по завесе делают то же. Раньше закрытие лишь прятало правки: они переживали его и записывались следующим «Сохранить настройки» — то есть на сервер уезжало то, что оператор считал брошенным. Это довод о целостности данных, а не о вкусе, и он же перевешивает риск случайной потери при клике мимо: у диалога один жест «уйти отсюда», и разное поведение у трёх его видов было бы хуже, чем у одного.

Дев-прокси Vite НЕ ставит changeOrigin, и это не упущение. Он переписывает Host на адрес бэкенда, а OriginProtectionMiddleware берёт из Host тот origin, с которым сверяет присланный браузером Origin; переписанный Host делает их разными. Проверка включается при наличии cookie сессии, поэтому первый вход в чистом браузере проходил, а дальше КАЖДЫЙ небезопасный запрос из дев-интерфейса отбивался 403 untrusted_origin — сохранение настроек, утверждение сценария, запуск кампании и сам повторный вход. На странице входа это читалось как «Неверные учётные данные», потому что форма ветвится на голом isError и не разбирает статус: под ту же надпись попадают 403, 429 (лимит попыток) и лежащий бэкенд. Разведение этих случаев осталось несделанным.

Числовое поле нейрошиллинга держит СВОЙ текст, пока его правят: пустая строка остаётся пустой и в черновик не уезжает, а на потере фокуса поле возвращает сохранённое значение. Раньше управляемое поле зажимало значение на каждом нажатии, а Number('') — ноль, поэтому стёртое поле мгновенно переписывалось нулём и следующие цифры дописывались к нему: «60» превращалось в «0180». Выход ЗА ГРАНИЦУ при этом зажимается сразу и виден сразу — там значение есть и оно недопустимо, а пустота это другое. Нативные стрелки type=number сняты классом tb-plain-number: Chrome резервирует под них место справа и только при наведении, из-за чего центрированное значение стоит мимо центра и дёргается — на паре полей «пауза от–до» они промахивались в разные стороны.

Редизайн нейрошиллинга добавил в дизайн-систему ровно то, чего она не умела выразить, а не то, что было удобно странице: залитый тон action у IconButton — для единственной иконочной кнопки, которая САМА является главным действием своего блока (остальные три тона говорят, что случится при нажатии, и рисуются только наведением, а этой надо быть видной до него); per-option disabled у SegmentedControl — его собственный комментарий уже признавал, что групповой флаг этого сказать не может, и единственный носитель из-за этого рисовал пару кнопок руками; ступень ширины sidebar — единственная, чьё значение диктует раскладка страницы, а не содержимое. Реакция в списке связей шага показывается ВЫКЛЮЧЕННОЙ, а не выбрасывается: реакция не сообщение, отвечать и реагировать на неё нечем, но дыра в нумерации («#1, #2, #3, #5») читалась как сбой, а не как правило.

Neurocomment audit 2026-09-02 (PR #427): of ~36 improvement proposals only 4 survived adversarial review — refused channel link (200 already_assigned) now toasts and keeps the input; Start disabled while the listener warms; reply mode rejects an answer echoing the quoted comment via the existing duplicate gate; three stale docstrings fixed. Rejected and NOT to be re-proposed without new operator pain: LLM fallback chain (#339 chose timeout+provider name), regeneration hints, per-account style (persona lives in the campaign prompt), token/cost accounting (non-goal, budget is in calls), campaign funnel endpoint (event feed already names every miss reason), liveness status fields, requeue on cooldown/over-cap (ponytail 'if it bites', test-pinned), inbox-expired event (live posts cannot outlive the 900s TTL), listener-deaf detector (5-min backfill re-attaches and re-reads), moving the logs purge out of warming (it runs at boot unconditionally), chip ready-ratio and hourly cap on the board (design port removed them), captcha queue details (#49/#330), splitting 700-line tests pre-emptively.

Closes two stale entries: the 2026-07-23 risk 'loses posts on overload/idle/restart' is resolved by the bounded SQLite inbox plus paged gap recovery (runtime-neurocomment.md); the 2026-08-05 decision reasoning about retry_pair is superseded by #330, which removed manual retry — re-linking the channel is the path that restores the captcha budget.

Временные статусы сессии (network_error, proxy_error, flood_wait, unknown_error) не блокируют готовность прогрева: evaluate_readiness режет только new и постоянные статусы через health_for_status == fail. Причина: снимок статуса от одной 75-секундной проверки во время мигания прокси парковал аккаунт при реконсиляции и перед каждым циклом до ручного клика, хотя цикл уже сам переживает провал set_online уходом в sleeping. Правду о сети выясняет первый шаг цикла, как и для flood_wait 2026-07-24. Отвергнуто: живой re-probe при реконсиляции (тот же гейт стоит перед каждым циклом, двойной RPC) и фоновая перепроверка раз в 10-15 минут (синхронный флот-RPC, который убирали в #202/#206).

Пул клиентов не повторяет лестницу подключения после транспортной ошибки: OSError (socket, timeout, python_socks) сразу поднимает TelegramClientPoolError. Причина: connect() Telethon уже делает connection_retries+1 = 4 попытки (~88 с, а не ~66 как раньше считал комментарий в config), и второй проход удваивал ожидание до ~176 с, пока все обращения к аккаунту стояли за _CONNECT_LOCKS. Повтор оставлен только для нетранспортных сбоев (занятый .session, RuntimeError), под которые он и был написан; комментарий про disconnect внутри _build_and_connect был устаревшим.

Массовое добавление аккаунтов сделано на клиенте поверх существующих import-session / import-tdata: каждый файл — свой запрос, батч-эндпоинта НЕТ и заводить его не надо. Один multipart с N сессиями упирается в лимит размера tdata, теряет прогресс и повтор по файлу и превращает один битый файл в перезалив всего пакета; при этом сервер уже умеет всё, что пакету нужно — атомарный импорт на архив, лок по имени сессии, отдельный staging на запрос. В полёте не больше двух файлов: каждый импорт тянет проверку сессии в Telegram на единственном uvicorn-воркере, пятьдесят параллельных — это не ускорение, а очередь на стороне Telegram.

Семантика пакета в мастере добавления: «Далее» ждёт весь пакет, а не первый успешный файл — иначе шаг прокси раздаёт прокси половине аккаунтов. Отмена посреди пакета останавливает очередь, но летящие запросы дают долететь и обновляют таблицу: аккаунт на сервере уже существует, и «забыть» о нём хуже, чем показать. В шаге пула клик по прокси отдаёт ему аккаунтов на все свободные слоты, а не одного; для одного аккаунта поведение прежнее — успех закрывает мастер, для многих закрытие всегда ручное, чтобы оператор прочитал счётчик «без прокси». Локальная поправка free привязана к снимку пула: рефетч после пакета уже содержит эти слоты, и вычитание дважды пряталo прокси со свободным слотом.
